title: Derived mate transport under a base-source isomorphism
statement: Choose derived categories of scheme modules [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $f:X\to S$, $g:S\prime\to S$, $g\prime:X\prime\to X$, $f\prime:X\prime\to S\prime$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $h:g\prime f=f\prime g$. For an isomorphism $e:S\prime\cong B$ and a witness $h_B:g\prime f=(f\prime e)(e^{-1}g)$, put $T=R(e^{-1})_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. There are natural isomorphisms $b:Rf\prime_*\cong R(f\prime e)_*\,T$ and $a:Rf_*\,Lg^*\cong Rf_*\,L(e^{-1}g)^*\,T$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] such that $\beta(h)_E\,b_{Lg\prime^*E}=a_E\,T(\beta(h_B)_E)$ for all $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, with the pinned mates [def-pc-derived-base-change-map]. The common codomain $S$ and the upper schemes are unchanged; the square need only commute.

proof.text: Use the selected pullback composition and identity isomorphisms to show L(e.inv) is an equivalence with inverse L(e.hom). Its pinned adjunction with T=R(e.inv) has invertible unit.

Put fB=fprime followed by e.hom. The comparison c fB e.inv followed by the equality fB e.inv=fprime gives cf:L(e.inv) followed by LfB ≅ Lfprime. Conjugate cf under the pinned adjunction for fprime and the composite of adj e.inv with adj fB to get b:Rfprime ≅ RfB followed by T. Insert the invertible adj e.inv unit after Lg, then compose c e.inv g and reassociate, and whisker with Rf to get a.

The private pullback_square_precomp lemma obtains LfB(c e.inv g) followed by qB = cf at Lg followed by q from pullback associativity and equality-transport naturality. The private domain_equivalence_transport lemma expresses b as a composite-adjunction Hom transpose and uses naturality to move the original mate through it. Substitute this square identity, expand the composite Hom equivalence into the two Hom equivalences, and use naturality under adj fB. The resulting transpose under adj e.inv is its unit followed by T of c e.inv g and then T of the new mate. This is exactly a followed by T of the new mate. No geometric or boundedness hypothesis is introduced.

theorem exists_derivedBaseChange_domain_iso
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g)
    {B : Scheme.{u}} (e : S' ≅ B)
    (hB : g' ≫ f = (f' ≫ e.hom) ≫ (e.inv ≫ g)) :
    let T := schemeDerivedDirectImage e.inv
    ∃ b : schemeDerivedDirectImage f' ≅
        schemeDerivedDirectImage (f' ≫ e.hom) ⋙ T,
    ∃ a : schemeDerivedDirectImage f ⋙ derivedPullback g ≅
        schemeDerivedDirectImage f ⋙ derivedPullback (e.inv ≫ g) ⋙ T,
      ∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
        schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' h E ≫
            b.hom.app ((derivedPullback g').obj E) =
          a.hom.app E ≫ T.map
            (schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f (f' ≫ e.hom) (e.inv ≫ g) g' hB E)
